page: Microsoft Azure L32as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled across the x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation sits at 256 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio with 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. Storage is bundled directly via 8024 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, while no dedicated graphics processing units are present.

Benchmark testing demonstrates robust baseline performance across compute and memory workloads. The instance registers a strong result in stress-ng single-core execution (2847.38) and PassMark memory performance (2852.32), complemented by top-quartile Geekbench image processing marks (14374.0). Multi-core benchmarks align solidly within the median tier, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 14326.0, PassMark CPU score of 38269.27, and stress-ng multi-core performance of 43243.72. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 79.55 GB/sec for uncached 256MB block reads and 45.38 GB/sec for sequential writes, supporting 31.8 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 22.77 GB/sec in static web serving.

The dense pairing of 8024 GB NVMe SSD storage and 256 GB of system RAM provides notable cost efficiency for disk-intensive and cache-heavy deployments without requiring external storage attachments. However, architectural tradeoffs exist: the lack of AVX-512 and matrix extensions limits acceleration for intensive vector workloads, reflected in lower-tier results for large 70B parameter LLM prompt processing (6.58 tokens/sec). The absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses also necessitates structured virtual network configurations.

Given its massive direct-attached NVMe storage array, balanced multi-core throughput, and substantial memory allocation, the L32as_v3 instance is specifically matched to high-IOPS transactional databases, large-scale NoSQL data stores, distributed caching layers, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L32as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) via an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked up to 3.525 GHz. It integrates 256 GB of RAM alongside 8024 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, operating without dedicated GPUs. In standardized testing, the instance exhibits top-quartile performance in single-core stress-ng tests, PassMark memory benchmarks, and Geekbench image processing, alongside median ratings across multi-core compute, Redis transactional throughput (31.8 million ops/sec), and web serving. While architectural boundaries like the absence of AVX-512 constrain high-parameter AI inference, the substantial local disk footprint and 8 GB per vCPU memory density offer strong qualitative value for I/O-intensive workloads. It is ideal for large relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, data warehousing, and intensive transactional operations.
